steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square baking pan.
Stir flour, baking powder, and salt together in a medium bowl.
Stir sugar, melted butter, and vanilla together in a large bowl.
Add one egg and mix with a spoon until well incorporated. Repeat to add remaining 2 eggs, mixing well after each addition.
Gradually add flour mixture and stir the batter until evenly moistened. Pour 1/2 of the batter back into the medium bowl that held the flour mixture.
Stir chocolate chips and cocoa into one bowl of batter. Stir pumpkin puree, walnuts, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg into the second bowl of batter.
Spread 1/2 of the chocolate batter into the bottom of the prepared baking pan, and follow with 1/2 of the pumpkin batter. Repeat the two layers once more.
Drag a kitchen knife or small spatula gently through the layers in a swirling motion to create a marbled appearance.
Bake in the preheated oven until the brownies begin to pull away from the sides of the pan, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 40 to 45 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool in the pan before cutting into 16 squares.
Serve warm, topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Brownies
raw_recipe.description: These fudgy pumpkin brownies are the perfect combination of chocolate, pumpkin puree, walnuts, and fall spices swirled together for a decadent treat!

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make a delicious brownie that's bursting with the flavors of fall. This homemade brownie batter gets layered with a pumpkin-spiced batter. Just swirl the two together and bake until a toothpick comes out clean. We suggest garnishing with whipped cream or ice cream for the full dessert experience.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! We love these. Followed the recipe, using canned organic pumpkin, mini chocolate chips and baked them in mini muffin tins. I used a small ice-cream scoop and just layered the two mixtures (did not swirl). The bake time was approx 23 min in my oven. At 18 minutes, I sprinkled additional mini choc chips and chopped walnuts on top and returned to the oven for the last 5 minutes. Perfect, delicious little bites that definately taste like autumn. By not swirling the two batters together, I think the pumpkin flavor really came through. Perfectly spiced, moist, and slightly dense. We really enjoyed these and will make them again. Thanks for sharing!

GREAT recipe. Flavors are perfect together. Only thing is (and many people mentioned this) that the chocolate batter is really thick while the pumpkin batter is thin. Not a problem except for spreading and swirling. I even put more "batter" in with the chocolate mixture, didn't help much. I ended up just doing chocolate on the bottom and pumpkin on top, swirled a little and poured a little caramel sauce over. Yum!

These were truly addictive! I made mini-muffins for a work pitch-in. I used mini choc chips instead of the regular sized chips. Suggestion: putting the pumpkin mixture in first, then the brownie makes it easier to remove the muffins. I baked them at 350 for 9 min, sprinkled a small amount of pecan chips/mini choc chips on top, then baked for another 9 minutes. Let them cool for about 15 min. Very cute presentation and so, so, SO delicious!

One of the best desserts I’ve made and I’ve been baking for 50 years! A few changes: In addition to baking powder, I added 1/2 tsp baking soda, I reduced sugar to 1 cup, I only had 1/3 cup chocolate chips which is enough, I put all of chocolate layer on bottom of 8”x8” pan with pumpkin layer on top. Instead of folding walnuts into pumpkin layer, I sprinkled 1/2 cup chopped pecans on top. They toasted beautifully. These bars are creamy, rich, delicious. It’s 5 a.m. the day after baking. I’m wondering how long I can resist eating one today.

This is REALLY close to Martha Stewart's recipe for pumpkin swirl brownies. Hers calls for only 1/2 cup of butter, 1 more egg and 1/4 tsp of cayenne. Otherwise they're fundamentally the same. That said, they ARE excellent brownies!

This is good but as noted in other reviews the part with the cocoa gets way to stiff. I split the batter 2/3 chocolate and 1/3pumpkin and added 2 tbsp milk to the chocolate part. I also made a batch with vegetable oil instead of melted butter and that helped you. But good taste overall.

Nice dessert for fall. I doubled this and poured into a 9x13 pan, took about 45 min. to bake and ended up being more cake-like. However, I made the mistake of not adding the flour until I had divided the batter in half and had added my cocoa/chips to some of it. This worked out well though as I had read where some thought the cocoa half was too thick and the pumpkin half too thin. So, I just added less flour to the cocoa half and more to the pumpkin half to work that out. I realized the cocoa half was still pretty thick so I thinned it out a bit with an extra 2/3 C. of pumpkin puree. Oh, I only used 2 C. of the 3 C. of sugar called for in the recipe. Next time I would probably decrease that to 1 1/2 C and decrease the chips to 3/4 C as well. Our family doesn't like our desserts too sweet. Ended up with a scrumptiously moist fall dessert!
I used Ghirardelli Chocolate Premium Brownie Mix Double Chocolate instead of making brownies. I layered brownie, pumpkin and more brownie. Added pecans and swirled. Fabulous! And easy!! Big hit!

These were a big favorite with everyone I shared them with. I baked them in a cupcake pan, for 30 minutes. I probably should've left them in for 5 more minutes, as a few of them had parts of the bottom come off, as those weren't fully set. The comments I received was that they were very moist and delicious. I didn't have walnuts, so used pecans instead, and I used Dutch processed cocoa as well. (and yes, I might use cupcake papers next time, or just extend the time as I mentioned previously.) Will make again!

So yummy! I am a big fan of pumpkin anything and this adds a nice switch up to the regular brownie. I added some applesauce to cut back the butter and some honey to substitute some sugar. I also did as suggested and gave a little more batter to the chocolate side. I used mini muffin pans so I just layered choc. Pumpkin. Choc. And about 23-25mins. Worth a try for any pumpkin fan!

I made these for my mother-in-law who loves pumpkin, and my father-in-law who loves chocolate. Only two things I did differently was make them in a 9x13 pan and the bottom layer was the only one with chocolate chips. Then I alternated pumpkin and chocolate. They were a huge hit! Once they were cool I put them in the fridge; I preferred them that way. This recipe is going into my "must have for fall" binder!
LOVED IT

Amazing with some little adjustments. I LOVED THESE. Great texture (weird straight out of the oven- let them cool!)! Things I did differently: Instead of the 1 1/2 cup sugar I did 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Works the same with less unnecessary sugar! I replaced the salt with espresso powder 9x9 instead of 8x8 and forget the excessive layering. Just put the chocolate layer then the pumpkin layer on top. Left out the nuts. I added some cookie dough bites to the topof half the batch, just for fun
This was very good. I subbed cranberries for the walnuts and added cardamom, otherwise followed the recipe. It would be _fantastic_ if recipes were by weight and not volume.
Made as directed. We didn’t like it at all. Not enough flavor and just not good. Threw most of it away.
Really easy to make as a beginner. I suggest using 1/2 cup of sugar instead and lowering the butter by a bit too.
These were great but I learned that I don’t really like pumpkin with chocolate lol It’s a 5 star recipe though, for sure
New holiday favorite!!! Everyone loved them!
These are the perfect blend of chocolate and pumpkin. Perfect texture. Perfect moisture level. So, so good!
They looked good and I followed the recipe exactly but the pumpkin layer came out really kind of mushy. The flavor is great! I'll make them again but will not marble them, Ill mix it all in one bowl.
